tools.description: Confirm a secret that the user filled on another device, with the confirmation code that the user read from their page. Only the user knows this code; never guess it.

code.description: The confirmation code exactly as the user read it from their page, for example 7KQ-2XRA.

tools.name: confirm_secret

tools.description: Erase a named secret and cancel its open request. Returns forgotten or missing.
tools.name: forget_secret

tools.description: Send an HTTPS request that uses one or more secrets by name, written as {{secret:NAME}} in a header, the URL query, or the body. The binary checks each secret's policy, sends the request, and returns the response with every secret value removed. In the URL query and in a form body (Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded), the value is URL-encoded; in a JSON body, it is JSON-escaped, so write {{secret:NAME}} inside the quotes. The request must use at least one secret.

method.description: HTTP method, for example GET or POST.

url.description: An https URL. {{secret:NAME}} may appear only in the query.

headers.description: Request headers. Values may contain {{secret:NAME}}, for example Authorization: Bearer {{secret:STRIPE_KEY}}.

body.description: Request body as text. May contain {{secret:NAME}}.

tools.name: http_request

tools.description: List ready secret metadata and pending requests, including remote confirmation.
tools.name: list_secrets

tools.description: Get the settings that route one command's HTTPS requests through the local secrets proxy, for tools such as curl or an SDK that cannot use http_request. The command writes {{secret:NAME}} where the secret goes; the proxy checks the policy, adds the value, and removes it from responses. Prefer http_request when it can do the task.
tools.name: proxy_settings

tools.description: Request a credential with a name and policy. Reports status and presentation; repeated calls with the same name and policy rejoin the request.

name.description: Name for the secret, for example STRIPE_KEY. Letters, digits, and underscores; starts with a letter.

reason.description: One sentence that tells the user why the secret is needed.

hosts.description: Exact host names that may receive the secret, for example api.stripe.com. A wildcard is allowed only as the first label, for example *.example.com.

methods.description: HTTP methods allowed, for example GET and POST. Leave out to allow any method.

paths.description: URL path patterns allowed, for example /v1/charges or /v1/customers/*. Leave out to allow any path.

policy.description: Where the secret may be sent. Ask for the narrowest policy that does the task.

expires_in_minutes.description: How long the request stays open, 1 to 60 minutes. Default 10.

tools.name: request_secret

tools.description: Request 2 to 8 secrets together in one local browser form, for example username and password. One submit publishes all fields atomically with a shared policy. Repeat identical arguments to rejoin. Wait with the request name; forgetting the group or any member erases the whole group. Phone/headless relay fill is not supported for groups.

name.description: Unique request name, for example LOGIN. Distinct from every field name. Use this name to wait or forget the entire group.

secrets.description: 2 to 8 secret fields. Each has a unique name for use by tools and an optional plain-text label. All values stay hidden from the agent.

reason.description: One sentence explaining why these credentials are needed.

hosts.description: Exact host names that may receive the secret, for example api.stripe.com. A wildcard is allowed only as the first label, for example *.example.com.

methods.description: HTTP methods allowed, for example GET and POST. Leave out to allow any method.

paths.description: URL path patterns allowed, for example /v1/charges or /v1/customers/*. Leave out to allow any path.

policy.description: One narrow policy shown to the human for every field.

expires_in_minutes.description: Request deadline, 1 to 60 minutes. Default 10. Filled values remain until forgotten or the session ends.

tools.name: request_secrets

tools.description: Run one command with secrets in its environment after browser approval or owner-enabled host authorization (Claude Code permission prompt or Codex approval policy). Use it only when a program must read a secret from its environment; prefer http_request. Pass an explicit absolute dir for client approval. A command that holds a secret can send it anywhere; its network policy is not enforced. Returns the exit code and the output with every secret value removed. Calling again with the same arguments rejoins an open approval.

command.description: The program and its arguments, one item each. No shell is used, so pipes and variables are not expanded. Standard input is empty.

secrets.description: Secrets for the command's environment, each as NAME:ENV_VAR, for example DB_PASSWORD:PGPASSWORD.

dir.description: Working folder. Default is the folder where the MCP server started.

tools.name: run_with_secret

tools.description: Wait for an existing request by name. Cannot open a page or change policy. Returns lifecycle state within the configured timeout.
tools.name: wait_for_secret
